question: In 2020, the percentage of wind power in the European Union’s electricity production stood at 14.2 %. The Council of Ministers expects each Member State to boost this proportion in the coming years, so that by 2030, 27 % of electricity will be generated from wind power.

The Commission is pursuing its so-called ‘green’ policy and is preparing to adopt one of the wind power action plans that it presented in October 2023. The aim of the plan is to reform the process of issuing calls for tenders by stressing the introduction of ‘non-price award criteria’, since this is currently the primary criterion when selecting project developers.

Under the new procedure, factors such as carbon content, reducing the environmental footprint and a longer life-time of installations must be taken into consideration in wind sector public procurement. In light of the above, could the Commission respond to the following questions: 1.
What consequences might these changes have on the price of electricity generated by the wind industry?
What measures does the Commission intend to take to guarantee transparency in this new procedure?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (2.5.2024) Member State can decide to include non-price criteria, whether as pre-qualification or as award criteria, to pursue additional policy objectives next to the sourcing of electricity at the lowest costs. These policy objectives may pursue increasing energy system integration or the protection of the environment and bring value added to society as a whole.

Proper auction design and implementation is key to ensure that this does not result in undue cost increases of the support measures or reduce competition. The inclusion of non-price criteria does not affect the wholesale price of electricity. The large majority of these non-price criteria are fixed costs which do not affect the marginal costs of generation.

The short-term marginal cost of production of electricity from wind remains very low and close to zero, whether non-price criteria are included in the auction or not. The marginal cost of the last unit introduced in the electricity system sets the wholesale electricity price.

How the inclusion of non-price criteria in a support scheme affects the cost of end users depends on how Member States finance the support scheme. EU legislation establishes obligations that support for electricity from renewable sources should be granted in an open, transparent, competitive, non-discriminatory and cost-effective manner.

This is also applicable for the use of non-price criteria in tenders This is regulated as such in Article 4 of the Renewable Energy Directive1, Article 19b of the Electricity Regulation2 and in the State aid rules3.

The Commission has also set State aid criteria to guarantee a level playing field in auction design4 and set out specific requirements in relation to non-price award criteria laid down in several State aid instruments.
